title: A running intentd cannot say which build it is, and status reads like it answered that
body:
**NOTHING ON THIS MACHINE CAN ASK A RUNNING `intentd` WHICH BUILD IT IS**, and `intent daemon status` answers a question next to that one -- _is it answering_ -- in a way that reads like the whole answer.

## What it cost, on 2026-09-04

A store-growth defect (`0234`) was fixed and committed at 16:01. The shared release pair had been built at 10:49 and nobody rebuilt it, so **every binary on the fleet still carried the defect while the repo did not.** In that state:

- I reported to hv that the binary on `PATH` already carried the fix. It did not. My check was `strings <bin> | grep -c "delete-all\|VALUES('rebuild')"`, which returned `2` -- **both matches were the pre-existing string `delete-all`, and the count was never about the fix at all.**
- hv ran `intent daemon stop && intent daemon start` expecting the fix to go live. It restarted the same 10:49 image. **Nothing in the output could have said so**: `ok: intentd is answering at ...` is true of a correct daemon and of a stale one in exactly the same words.
- The restart was run a second time after the rebuild, and establishing that THAT one picked up the new code took `pgrep` + `ps -o lstart` + `lsof -p <pid>` + `stat` on the artefact + `strings` -- five commands, none of them about intentd, to answer a question intentd knows the answer to.

`intent --version` prints its own commit sha (`intent 3.0.0 (28c1c094e)`). **The daemon has the same information and no way to be asked for it.**

## Why `status` is the wrong home for the fix, stated because it is the obvious one

Adding a sha to `daemon status` would help, and it would leave the deeper shape in place: **the operator has to know to ask.** The failure above is not that somebody asked and got a bad answer; it is that _the daemon is answering_ was taken as sufficient, correctly, because it is what the verb is called.

The property worth reporting is not the daemon's version but the AGREEMENT between three things that can silently disagree: the running image, the artefact on disk, and `HEAD`. Today all three differed and every individual reading was correct.

## Suggested shape, not a specification

`daemon status` reports the running image's sha and says plainly when it differs from the artefact on disk -- _running 10:49 build; a newer binary is on disk, restart to pick it up_. A daemon that has been superseded is the normal case after any rebuild, so this is a routine line rather than an error.

Worth considering alongside: the gate already prints `N non-test file(s) under native/rust changed since <sha> -- this binary is behind HEAD`, which is the same question asked about the CLI. **That line exists and the daemon has no equivalent**, so the coverage is half of a pair rather than a missing feature.

## Not measured

- Whether `intentd` currently records its own build sha anywhere reachable at runtime, or would need one embedded.
- Whether any other long-lived process on this estate has the same gap.
